A1.justification: Both PDFs describe CoMPaSS, its SCOP and TENOR components, and the same four diffusion backbones. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite substantial reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original text-encoder retrieval tests, image-generation evaluations, component ablations, and runtime measurements in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains the original empirical studies and adds human validation, DPG-Bench evaluations, efficiency and sensitivity experiments, and three-object composition results.

M1.justification: The standard SCOP/TENOR procedure, attention supervision, and LoRA setup are retained. V2 adds a targeted adaptation: further fine-tuning FLUX.1+CoMPaSS on size-contrast data filtered through an adapted SCOP engine (Figure 7). This additional training stage is absent from v1.

E1.justification: V2 adds DPG-Bench's long, dense prompts and a constructed benchmark of 512 three-object spatial prompts (Appendix C.4), extending evaluation beyond the retained coverage. Figure 7 also tests explicit extreme size disparities. The original COCO-derived training dataset remains.

E2.justification: V2 adds evaluated comparisons with R&B, Attention Refocusing, and Layout Guidance in the computational-efficiency study (Table 3), substantially broadening comparison to inference-only approaches. These comparisons concern overhead, not image-generation accuracy. The existing main and appendix VISOR comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: V2 introduces a 500-image training control preserving category and relationship distributions, three-object evaluation with any/all correctness measures, and training/inference time and VRAM comparisons excluding bounding-box generation. It also adds human validation and a 100-step, batch-size-4 adaptation experiment. The original training hyperparameter table is unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds SCOP threshold sensitivity tests, reduced-data experiments, human validation of curated pairs, three-object generalization analysis, and a size-disparity failure case with targeted mitigation. These test robustness, data efficiency, curation quality, and applicability boundaries beyond v1's retained component ablations.

E5.justification: Appendix B retains the same latency measurements and accompanying ± values. V2 introduces no new run-count, seed, confidence-interval, or significance-testing information. Its human-agreement percentage is an additional evaluation outcome without uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Matched original benchmark, fidelity, ablation, and latency values remain unchanged. Substantial new results include DPG-Bench overall scores of 80.63/84.42 and three-object all-correct rates of 13.1%/31.2% for base/CoMPaSS-enhanced FLUX.1, respectively. V2 also adds human agreement of 85.2%, efficiency and sensitivity results, and new qualitative examples.

T1.justification: The five formal SCOP constraints and their mathematical definitions in Equations 1–5 are unchanged. V2 adds explanatory discussion of TENOR's role, but no new formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The three central contributions and headline gains of +98%, +67%, and +131% are retained. V2 refines TENOR's advertised role from preserving spatial semantics to preserving token order and linguistic structure, consistent with its clarified division of responsibilities between TENOR and SCOP.

C2.justification: V2 explicitly separates TENOR's structural signal from the semantic grounding supplied by SCOP (Section 3.2). Its new limitations discussion identifies viewer-centric scope, unsupported object-centric frames, contextual spatial language, and extreme size-disparity failures. V1 contains no comparable treatment of these applicability boundaries.

D1.justification: Code changes from promised to stated available. V2 identifies grid search, clarifies internal descriptors and crop perturbation, and supplies the targeted adaptation budget. The main training table is retained, but v1's explicit VISOR detector and four-images-per-prompt description is omitted. Some new study procedures remain sparsely specified.

R1.justification: V2 substantially expands positioning around reinforcement learning, preference optimization, training-based versus inference-only control, and qualitative spatial relations. It adds substantive references such as R&B and spatial-representation research. These additions go beyond the numerous bibliographic publication updates.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, related work, method explanations, and experimental narrative. It consolidates training documentation in the appendix, reorganizes evaluation subsections, and replaces the conclusion section with Discussion and Conclusion. Appendix organization and captions are also revised.

P2.justification: V2 merges spatial and fidelity results into an expanded Table 2, moves and extends the detailed benchmark table as Table A11, and adds several experimental displays. Figure 1 is replaced, Figure 7 is new, and Table 1 and Figure 6 are substantially compressed. The original appendix image galleries are retained under new numbering.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens evidence for compositional generalization through long-prompt and three-object evaluations. Data-budget controls, sensitivity tests, and computational comparisons better substantiate the framework's practical claims, while the clarified mechanism and explicit failure boundaries improve scientific precision. These gains outweigh the loss of some VISOR protocol detail and incomplete specification of parts of the new studies; the original benchmark and ablation evidence is preserved.
